summary: Two complementary routes are supported by the inspected official sources. CMS hospital cost reports provide annual, facility-level bed and utilization context; HCUP NEDS provides a national ED-discharge benchmark, including separate ED and inpatient supplemental files. Neither supplies New Brunswick hourly census, staffed-bed status, admission-decision times, boarding intervals, or bed-cleaning times. Treat both as contextual inputs and keep operational time distributions uncalibrated until an approved institutional aggregate extract is available.

sources.title: Hospital Provider Cost Report Data and API documentation
sources.geography: United States; facility-level records keyed by CMS Certification Number (CCN), including candidate CCNs 310038 and 310070 subject to record verification
sources.period: Annual cost-report periods; the inspected API documentation page did not expose the current available-year range
sources.grain: Hospital/facility and annual cost-report period; not unit-, event-, or hourly-level
useful_fields: Number of Beds For Adults & Peds
Total Bed Days Available For Adults & Peds
inpatient days and discharges where available in the public-use-file subset
observed_facts: The CMS API documentation search result identifies the dataset endpoint pattern /dataset/{uuid}/data and lists adult-and-pediatric beds and total bed days available.
CMS describes hospital cost reports as annual provider reports and says the public-use file is a subset of HCRIS variables.
The data dictionary defines beds as beds available for patient lodging at period end and bed days as beds available over the reporting period; these are not staffed-bed or hourly occupancy measures.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Open the CMS dataset landing page and API documentation; identify the current dataset UUID and exact API/download URLs from CMS-provided links. Query only CCNs 310038 and 310070 and a bounded, explicitly selected set of annual periods. Preserve each facility’s reporting-period start/end dates and source release. Do not infer licensed or staffed capacity from the reported bed count.
limitations: Annual facility aggregates cannot parameterize hourly census, ED boarding, bed turnover, or unit-level capacity.
The inspected API page did not render field-level content, so endpoint UUID, direct download URL, and current year coverage require independent verification.
Public-use-file fields are a subset of cost-report data; omissions must not be interpreted as zero.

sources.title: Nationwide Emergency Department Sample (NEDS) File Specifications
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project
sources.geography: United States; national sample, not identifiable New Brunswick or Middlesex County facilities
sources.period: Annual datasets; the inspected specifications page documents 2023 and earlier years
sources.grain: ED visit/discharge records, with separate hospital weights, supplemental ED and supplemental inpatient files
useful_fields: ED visit disposition and admission-related indicators in core-file layout (verify exact names in the selected year's record layout)
ED supplemental file variables (verify exact time and clinical fields in annual layout)
hospital weights and hospital characteristics in separate hospital file
observed_facts: AHRQ describes each annual NEDS as a core CSV plus hospital-weights, supplemental ED, and supplemental inpatient files; a diagnosis/procedure-groups file is available beginning in 2018.
The official page lists 2023 files with 31,003,348 core records, 963 hospital records, and 26,458,415 ED supplemental records.
NEDS is a national sample. These record counts do not identify local hospital flow or establish a local service-time distribution.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Use the annual file specifications and record layouts to select one bounded year (for example, 2023) and verify whether any ED duration/time variables are present before seeking data. Obtain the applicable HCUP files through its documented access route and follow required training/data-use terms; filter only to a defensible national or regional benchmark stratum, retain survey weights, and report disposition-specific summaries. Treat observed aggregate ED duration measures as outcomes, not direct service-time distributions.
limitations: NEDS is not a public direct-download microdata file; access requires HCUP's applicable purchase/access process and data-use conditions.
National sampled records cannot calibrate either New Brunswick ED without local evidence.
Annual layout changes require field-name and definition checks for the selected year; exact fields were not independently opened in this bounded search.

sources.title: HCUPnet Data Tools
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project
sources.geography: National and regional community-hospital estimates; county population tables also available, but not facility-specific Middlesex County flow
sources.period: Annual HCUP data years; page documents 2023 NIS changes and has ED and inpatient tools
sources.grain: Query-generated aggregate tables and graphs by available setting, geography, and selectable characteristics
useful_fields: ED and inpatient utilization measures exposed by selected dashboard
disposition or admission categories where available in selected table
patient-location and regional strata subject to year-specific availability
observed_facts: AHRQ says HCUPnet generates tables and graphs for national and regional community-hospital statistics across inpatient, ED, and population-based county settings.
The tool provides a download of the selected visualization as an Excel file.
For 2023, patient-residence metro classification is consolidated to metropolitan versus non-metropolitan, limiting continuity with earlier detailed categories.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Use the public dashboard to define one national or regional ED/inpatient table, record all selected filters and data year, and download the resulting Excel table. Retain the selected measure definitions and query configuration with the file. Use the result only as an external aggregate benchmark, not as a New Brunswick estimate.
limitations: The tool does not provide hourly event traces, bed readiness, staffed capacity, or facility-specific flow for the two named hospitals.
Available strata and definitions differ across years; preserve the query-year caveats.
An aggregate table cannot yield a defensible within-visit service-time distribution.

missing_inputs: Approved facility-level aggregates for New Brunswick ED arrival and disposition counts by hour and acuity.
Admission decision, ED departure, inpatient bed assignment/arrival, and bed-cleaning timestamps or interval summaries, with censored observations and transfer destinations defined.
Time-varying physical, licensed, staffed, and open beds by unit; these capacity concepts must be reported separately.
A current CMS cost-report API UUID, direct download URL, exact current annual coverage, and verified field layout for the two CCNs.
Verified annual HCUP record-layout fields and definitions for any candidate ED time variables before acquisition.
simulation_use: Use CMS annual beds and bed days only as historical facility-level context after confirming the two CCN records and report periods. Use HCUPnet or properly accessed NEDS only for external disposition and utilization benchmarks with geography, year, weighting, and access limitations explicitly carried into the simulation. Do not convert median ED duration into a service-time distribution. For ED-to-bed flow, request a bounded institutional aggregate specifying arrival-to-admission-decision, decision-to-ED-departure, departure-to-inpatient-bed-arrival, and bed-vacated-to-clean-ready intervals, stratified by acuity and disposition, including counts, quantiles, timestamp coverage, and right-censoring rules.
limitations: Research discovery only; no dataset was acquired or locally validated.
The inspected official sources do not provide local hourly census or live bed availability.
All candidates require independent source-scope, rights, field-definition, and domain-applicability review before incorporation.
